response.markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize **terminal-prefix candidate-softmax training** for the supplied BERT4Rec. No validation improvement has been measured; treat masking and loss changes as separate hypotheses.

**Insights.** From the starting point: (1) terminal prefixes align with appended-mask inference but do not automatically teach recency; (2) title-confusable negatives may distinguish specific matches but can be valid alternatives; (3) ordinary Cloze retains supervision across histories. From related work: (1) BERT4Rec describes final-item training, although its released generator differs; (2) gSASRec motivates loss ablation without establishing benefits for BERT4Rec; (3) sampled-softmax analyses require distinguishing candidate classification from full-softmax estimation. These suggest inference alignment, competitive ranking, and temporal relevance as research directions.

**Framework.** Organize methods by the component they change:

| Component | Foundation | Proposed experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Training context | BERT4Rec; Recency Sampling | Cloze plus explicitly recent terminal prefixes |
| Ranking objective | gSASRec; sampled-softmax analysis | Uniform, distinct multi-negative candidate softmax |
| Attention | MEANTIME; TiSASRec | Learned relative-position/time biases |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are O/F/U/M/D: originality, future potential, user alignment, model alignment, implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Alignment scores express hypotheses, not demonstrated effects.

- **Terminal-prefix candidate softmax: 4/7/7/8/4.** O: useful combination; established components. F: reusable controlled recipe; gains may saturate. U: recent targets and competition address stale-interest revival and broad matches outranking direct connections; ownership remains unobserved. M: targets weak separation; training margins cannot establish HR@10. D: local changes; normalization and sampling need care.
- **Temporal attention biases: 5/7/7/5/6.** O: adapts established mechanisms; limited novelty. F: transferable; timestamps may be sparse. U: distinguishes temporal evidence; gaps do not establish fulfillment. M: conditions representations; no measured temporal defect. D: feasible attention changes; timestamp plumbing expands scope.
- **Moderate title-negative sampling: 4/6/7/7/5.** O: practical adaptation; familiar mining. F: targets confusability; false negatives constrain benefits. U: challenges broad similarity; titles cannot verify compatibility. M: harder comparisons; noisy negatives can hurt. D: feasible retrieval; filtering adds complexity.

**Selected algorithm.** Retain one BERT4Rec per category. Mix Cloze with suffix-free terminal prefixes, sampling recent training targets explicitly. Normalize each objective separately; sample 64 distinct eligible negatives. Preserve the baseline optimizer and architecture.

This targets two user failures—reviving older isolated interests and ranking broad matches above direct recent connections—and Electronics’ weakest sampled separation: 6.62% negative-beats-positive. These links are hypotheses; neither margins nor embedding cosine establish recommendation quality, diversity, or compatibility.

Keep seeds, splits, routing, 200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch fixed. Predeclare a 2×2 masking/loss ablation, checkpoint cadence and equal compute caps; never combine predictions. Record target counts and updates. Select by pinned macro validation HR@10; paired category-stratified bootstraps, if host hit indicators are available, describe conditional uncertainty without removing selection bias. Preserve diagnostic definitions and predictor consistency.

idea.description: Train each category’s single BERT4Rec with separately normalized ordinary Cloze and recent terminal-prefix objectives. Evaluate uniform multi-negative candidate softmax independently of the masking change through a predeclared 2×2 ablation. Defer semantic mining and architectural changes until this simpler hypothesis has been evaluated.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies older isolated interests being revived and broadly related items outranking direct recent-interest matches. Explicitly recent terminal targets emphasize contemporary next-choice contexts; competition among multiple candidates may improve discrimination. These mechanisms do not guarantee either behavioral improvement and cannot establish ownership, exact compatibility, or whether a need has been fulfilled. Electronics has the weakest measured sampled separation: a 0.7269 lower-tail margin and 6.62% negative-beats-positive rate. The embedding scores indicate modest directional similarity, not severe collapse or recommendation diversity. Positive margins against individual training negatives do not establish ranking quality against the host’s 99 negatives.
idea.implementation_notes:
Apply changes inside the supplied corrected baseline, retaining its BERT4Rec backbone, optimizer, architecture, preprocessing and category routing. This is a proposed experiment, not executable replacement code or a claim of measured gains.

Reproducible example construction: sample uniformly with replacement from category training users having at least two interactions. Use only their training histories. For a history of length n, eligible terminal indices are t=1,...,n-1, indexed from zero. Choose t uniformly from the most recent min(10,n-1) eligible indices. The constant 10 is a proposed hyperparameter, not a research-established optimum. Construct history[max(0,t-(L-1)):t] followed by the reserved MASK and left-pad to length L. The target is history[t]; omit its complete future suffix. This aligns terminal prediction with inference while explicitly favoring recent targets. Uniform arbitrary-prefix sampling alone would not justify a recency claim.

For the Cloze component, retain the corrected baseline’s exact history windowing and corruption implementation in every ablation cell and record its mask rate and target-selection rules in the run manifest. The baseline implementation was not supplied here, so its numerical mask rate must not be invented. Every supervised target must be completely replaced by MASK; do not apply an unchanged-token corruption option that exposes its identity through bidirectional input. Ensure at least one supervised position per eligible Cloze example. If correcting a target-exposure defect were necessary, apply that correction to all cells before comparison.

Use a fixed 50:50 objective mixture, not an epoch curriculum. For batch size B>=2, construct max(1,floor(B/2)) terminal examples and the remaining Cloze examples, preserving the baseline total batch size. Within each objective, average losses over supervised positions; then compute loss=0.5*terminal_mean+0.5*cloze_mean. Thus a 50% objective weight does not depend on how many masks a Cloze example contains. This choice retains target weighting within each component; it is not per-example normalization. If one component has no valid supervised positions, use the other component alone and record the event; skip an update only if neither is valid. Report realized component counts because exclusions can alter exposure.

Candidate objective: for user u, define eligible negatives as catalog IDs excluding PAD, MASK and every item in that user’s complete training history, including all supervised positives. Never consult validation or test labels for exclusions. Sample uniformly without replacement with K=min(64,eligible_count), separately for each supervised position. Use all eligible items when eligible_count<64. Pad candidate arrays only for batching and mask unused logits to negative infinity. Skip supervised positions with no eligible negatives. Use bounded sampling or exact complement sampling rather than unbounded rejection loops. This is a deliberate unseen-item candidate-classification objective, not the original BERT4Rec full-catalog objective and not an unbiased approximation of it. No importance correction is claimed. Keep temperature 1.0 and equal positive/negative scoring conventions.

Memory: gather only supervised hidden states before scoring positive-plus-K candidates. Chunk embedding lookup and scoring to avoid materializing all M*K*hidden_dim intermediates. Accumulate loss sums and counts separately for terminal and Cloze components so chunking exactly preserves their objective weights. Do not silently average chunk means of unequal sizes.

Controlled experiment: predeclare four configurations crossing the corrected baseline masking versus the specified mixed masking with corrected baseline loss versus candidate softmax. Record the actual baseline loss rather than assuming it is single-negative BCE; original BERT4Rec used full softmax. Keep optimizer, architecture, batch size and all unrelated hyperparameters fixed. Each configuration trains four category models independently; configurations are compared and never fused. The selected configuration supplies exactly one checkpoint per category. No checkpoint averaging, independent experts or auxiliary fitted popularity/transition scores are allowed.

Budget and selection: retain preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches in each completed epoch. Use separate deterministically seeded RNG streams for user sampling, masking and negatives; record RNG implementation and states. Predeclare validation every 10 completed epochs and at completion, selecting the checkpoint with highest pinned macro validation HR@10 and breaking ties in favor of the earlier checkpoint. Account for every training, diagnostic and failed-run GPU second within the shared 43,200-second allowance. Divide the remaining allowance equally across the four cells, including their diagnostics; end compute-limited runs at completed epochs. Record actual epochs, updates, masked-target counts, elapsed GPU seconds and configuration manifests. Equal compute caps can yield unequal training exposure, so report both rather than claiming exact update matching. Do not add a separate baseline rerun if an eligible corrected cold-start measurement already supplies that cell; reserve its allocation rather than silently expanding other searches.

Use identical pinned validation users and candidate sets across configurations. If the host exposes per-user validation hit indicators, compute paired hit differences and bootstrap users with replacement independently within each category; average the four category differences per replicate, using a recorded bootstrap seed and 10,000 replicates. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals are conditional on fitted models and candidates, omit training-seed variability, and do not correct repeated-selection optimism or imply full-catalog gains. If hit indicators are unavailable, report the supplied aggregate scores without inventing uncertainty. Full-catalog recommendations for the twenty simulator users remain qualitative diagnosis, not an alternate selection metric.

Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), host ModelView interfaces, DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). view.model must remain the actual trained nn.Module. Diagnostic batches retain (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L, with valid MASK-position supervision and the original definitions. Keep a reproducible uniform diagnostic-negative stream distinct from optimization sampling, record measured-position counts, and do not reinterpret training margins as validation performance. Missing categories, ownership, reviews, ratings and simulator traits remain explicitly unavailable.

Inference retains the corrected baseline’s appended-MASK path: keep at most L-1 history items, append MASK, left-pad and gather the final nonpadding position using explicit position indices, never count-1. Exclude PAD and MASK from catalog outputs. No architecture change is required; nevertheless verify that the predictor writer emits the same architecture, configuration and state-dict loading used in training. Do not read other trials or reuse their checkpoints.

Risks and missing evidence: recent-target sampling may overweight popular items or transient behavior and suppress valid long-term interests. Uniform negatives can be easy or plausible unseen positives; excluding training positives does not resolve that ambiguity. Candidate loss may encourage popularity shortcuts or different logit scales, and raw margin thresholds are scale-sensitive. Compare the four predeclared cells and optionally report training-frequency and history-length strata from already available validation hit indicators; these are descriptive checks, not additional selection objectives. Titles alone cannot verify compatibility, and repeated validation selection remains a source of optimism. Temporal attention and semantic negatives remain deferred alternatives, not additional fitted scoring components.
idea.pseudocode:
Predeclare four cells: masking in {corrected_baseline, mixed_terminal_cloze}; loss in {corrected_baseline, candidate_CE}.
Fix seeds, optimizer, architecture, batch size, splits, routing, evaluation cadence, checkpoint rule and per-cell remaining-budget allocation.
For each cell, train one independent BERT4Rec per category; never combine cells or checkpoints.
For each completed epoch, run exactly 200 optimizer batches:
    Sample eligible training users uniformly with replacement using a recorded seeded RNG.
    If mixed masking:
        Build approximately half terminal and half baseline-Cloze examples.
        For each terminal history h of length n:
            recent_count = min(10, n-1)
            t = uniform_integer(n-recent_count, n-1), inclusive
            context = h[max(0, t-(L-1)):t]
            sequence = left_pad(context + [MASK], L)
            positive[terminal_MASK_position] = h[t]
            Omit every item after t and omit h[t] from the input at its target position.
    Otherwise:
        Use corrected baseline example construction unchanged.
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    Gather only supervised MASK-position features.
    If candidate_CE:
        For each supervised target belonging to user u:
            eligible = real_catalog_ids minus set(full_training_history[u])
            K = min(64, len(eligible))
            If K == 0: skip this target.
            negatives = uniform_sample_without_replacement(eligible, K)
            candidates = [positive] + negatives
            logits = model.predict_score(target_features, candidates)
            loss_at_target = cross_entropy(logits, target_index=0)
        Compute chunked sums and counts without changing weights.
    Otherwise:
        Apply the actual corrected-baseline loss at supervised positions.
    If mixed masking:
        loss = 0.5*mean_valid_terminal_loss + 0.5*mean_valid_cloze_loss
        If one component is empty, use the nonempty component alone and log it.
    Otherwise:
        Use the corrected baseline reduction.
    Update once unless no valid targets exist; record skipped batches separately.
Evaluate through the unchanged host protocol at the predeclared cadence.
Select checkpoints by fixed macro validation HR@10, breaking ties toward earlier epochs.
Compare all four cells; report component effects and interaction descriptively.
Deploy only the selected configuration's one checkpoint per category.
Emit matching appended-MASK inference through the existing predictor writer.
Run preserved family-specific diagnostics using their recorded definitions.

originality.positive: Combines explicitly recent terminal contexts, controlled objective normalization and candidate competition into a focused BERT4Rec experiment.
originality.negative: Final-item masking, recency sampling and candidate objectives are established; the proposed recipe is an adaptation rather than a new model principle.

future_potential.positive: The factorial comparison can reveal whether inference alignment, competitive supervision or their interaction warrants subsequent temporal or semantic research.
future_potential.negative: Transfer beyond this sampled-candidate benchmark is uncertain, and the available observations cannot resolve ownership, exact compatibility or current intent.

code_difficulty.positive: Preserves architecture and inference while concentrating changes in example construction, negative sampling and loss reduction.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct component weighting, bounded unique sampling, memory-safe scoring, reproducible RNG streams and budgeted comparisons require more care than a simple loss substitution.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item recommendation with full-softmax training.
Describes additional final-item masking examples to align training with appended-mask inference.
Provides the foundation for preserving masked targets and preventing bidirectional target exposure.
limitations: Already establishes final-item masking, limiting the proposed method's originality.
Does not establish the optimal recent-prefix distribution, mixture weight or candidate objective for this benchmark.
Task alignment alone does not demonstrate improved recency sensitivity.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec released data generator
contributions: Builds overlapping chronological windows anchored backward from history ends and duplicates them with random masks.
Distinguishes random-mask training with force_last=False from terminal masking of the latest window with force_last=True for evaluation.
limitations: Does not directly implement the paper's explicit terminal-only training mixture or arbitrary terminal-prefix sampling.
Its released behavior must not be assumed to match the host's corrected baseline.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec released trainer
contributions: Gathers supervised masked representations before output scoring.
Normalizes summed masked-target loss by valid-target count across a batch.
limitations: Target-count normalization gives examples with more masked targets greater contribution.
A terminal-example sampling probability therefore does not automatically equal its loss weight.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Examines overconfidence and optimization problems associated with negative-sampled BCE.
limitations: Its evidence concerns a different backbone and motivates, rather than validates, a BERT4Rec loss experiment.
It does not justify assuming that the supplied corrected baseline uses single-negative BCE.

related_work.title: Sampled-softmax analysis for recommendation
contributions: Analyzes sampling bias and differences between always-included positives and sampled negatives.
limitations: Does not make uncorrected candidate cross-entropy an unbiased full-catalog objective.
Does not establish the optimal negative count or exclusion policy for the supplied datasets.

related_work.title: MEANTIME
contributions: Provides a precedent for multiple temporal embeddings and differentiated attention within one jointly trained network.
limitations: Temporal modeling requires a consistent unknown-time convention for the inference mask.
Observed gaps do not establish ownership, fulfillment or present demand.
Its architectural changes are deferred to preserve the initial experiment's interpretability.

related_work.title: TiSASRec
contributions: Models item positions and pairwise time intervals in sequential attention.
Motivates distinguishing elapsed time from sequence distance.
limitations: Its causal backbone must not replace the required BERT4Rec family.
Temporal relevance in this benchmark remains an untested hypothesis.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling research
contributions: Supports investigating explicit recency-aware target selection across recommendation architectures.
limitations: Studies sampled-target removal and multiple-positive prediction rather than this BERT4Rec terminal-prefix mixture.
Does not establish a last-ten-target rule, a 50:50 mixture or an epoch curriculum.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can fail to preserve full-catalog model rankings.
limitations: Does not invalidate the mandated fixed benchmark; it limits interpretation beyond its sampled candidates.
Does not provide uncertainty estimates for the proposed fitted models.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit a finite validation criterion.
limitations: Predeclared comparisons reduce researcher flexibility but do not eliminate selection optimism.
Post-selection bootstrap intervals do not correct winner-selection bias.

related_work.title: TensorFlow uniform candidate sampler documentation
contributions: Documents candidate sampling behavior and the distinction between unique and repeated draws.
limitations: A sampler does not automatically implement the proposed user-specific training-positive exclusions.
Documentation informs implementation semantics rather than supplying recommendation-performance evidence.

related_work.title: TensorFlow sampled softmax loss documentation
contributions: Documents sampling-aware machinery used in sampled-softmax estimation.
limitations: Plain positive-plus-negative candidate cross-entropy is a different objective.
The proposed PyTorch implementation neither depends on TensorFlow nor claims equivalent corrections.
